clue.text: Church office secretary no slouch

parts.note: PA is a personal assistant, a secretary
someone who is no slouch is quick, and pacy means fast

explanation.surface: An office worker in a church is praised as being anything but lazy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Church office' reads as a place of work, but it is the office of Pope.
explanation.definitionFit: The papacy is the position held by the Pope, the highest office of the Roman Catholic Church.

clue.text: Fatal shot bags duck on the water

indicators.note: the shuffled letters capture the duck, holding it inside
shot means ruined or broken up, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: a duck is a score of nought in cricket, so O

explanation.surface: A hunter's fatal shot brings down a duck sitting on a pond.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shot' rearranges FATAL into AFLAT, and 'bags' places the O inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something afloat is floating, buoyed up and not sunk, so on the surface of the sea or a lake.

clue.text: Advanced clue for bid rejected

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for advanced, as in A level
read as words, the letters spell 'B and one D', itself a little clue for bid: B, then one (I), then D

explanation.surface: An auction bid that was put forward early is turned down.
explanation.walkthrough: The rest of the answer, read as words, is a little clue for BID: B and one (I) and D.
explanation.definitionFit: Something abandoned has been given up or deserted, cast aside as no longer wanted.

clue.text: All months not ending in R? Agreed

indicators.note: the final letter, the one named, is dropped from the end

parts.note: all twelve months make up a year

explanation.surface: A query about months lacking the letter R, as in the oyster rule, then assent.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface echoes the old saying that oysters should only be eaten in months with an R in them.
explanation.definitionFit: Yea is an old word for yes, the vote cast by someone who has agreed to a motion.

clue.text: Truthful answer given by Conservative minister

parts.note: a curate is a minister of the church, an assistant to a parish priest

explanation.surface: A Tory government minister responds honestly to a question.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minister' suggests a politician beside 'Conservative', but here it is a clergyman.
explanation.definitionFit: An accurate account is correct and faithful to the facts, so truthful in that sense.

clue.text: It's able to develop a flower

indicators.note: the letters develop, growing into a different form

explanation.surface: Something is capable of growing into a bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: Astilbe is a garden perennial with feathery plumes of tiny blossoms, a flowering plant.

clue.text: Where there's traffic when there's traffic

definitions.text: Where there's traffic when there's traffic

parts.words: Where there's traffic when there's traffic
parts.note: traffic in two senses: trading in goods, and the vehicles crowding the field where the selling happens out of their back ends

explanation.walkthrough: The repeated word is the joke: buying and selling take place among a crowd of parked cars. This kind of sale is a British market where people sell junk from their vehicles.
explanation.definitionFit: At this British event people sell secondhand goods from the backs of parked vehicles, so trading and cars meet.

clue.text: Baps in topless posters giving offence

indicators.note: topless means the first letter is removed, the top of a down answer

parts.note: trolls post deliberately offensive messages online

explanation.surface: Pictures of topless women on posters cause offence, with 'baps' as slang for breasts.
explanation.walkthrough: A bap is a British soft bread roll; the surface leans on its slang sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Baps are soft round bread buns, a kind of bread roll common in Britain.

clue.text: Silent predator bats want to screech

indicators.note: bats means crazy, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: to yowl is to cry out loudly, to screech

explanation.surface: A noiseless hunter in the night while bats squeal for something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bats' looks like animals sharing the night scene with the predator, but it signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Owls hunt almost silently thanks to soft-edged feathers, and this brown woodland species preys on small mammals.

clue.text: More charming petitions before king

parts.note: pleas are earnest requests, petitions
ante is Latin for before, as in antenatal
R is the abbreviation for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: Requests presented to a monarch are judged more appealing.
explanation.definitionFit: Pleasanter is the comparative of pleasant, meaning more agreeable or delightful.

clue.text: Heading west through Cornwall's green and pleasant land

indicators.note: in an across clue heading west means reading right to left, backwards
the letters wanted run through the middle of the word that follows

parts.note: the run of letters taken from inside this word

explanation.surface: A trip west through the English county of Cornwall, echoing Blake's 'green and pleasant land'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Green and pleasant land' is Blake's phrase for England (from the hymn Jerusalem); here it describes a garden patch. NWAL sits inside CORNWALL'S and turns round when read heading west.
explanation.definitionFit: A lawn is a stretch of mown grass, literally a green and pleasant piece of ground in a garden.

clue.text: Lord Chancellor Labour consider a wally

indicators.note: to labour something is to work it over, so these letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A political jibe: the Labour party thinks the Lord Chancellor is a fool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Labour' looks like the political party, but it is a verb telling you to work the letters of CONSIDER A WALLY into a new order. A wally is British slang for a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Wolsey, cardinal and statesman, served Henry VIII as Lord Chancellor of England until his fall in 1529.

clue.text: Singer in audio dubbing storm

indicators.note: in audio means as heard, so a word that sounds the same is used

parts.note: dubbing someone is knighting them with a sword, and a gale is a storm; said together they make the bird's name

explanation.surface: A vocalist records a soundtrack, dubbing a song about a storm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dubbing' looks like sound recording, but it is conferring a knighthood.
explanation.definitionFit: The nightingale is a songbird famous for its rich song, often sung at night.

clue.text: Government bound by new vote for oversight

indicators.note: the government letter is tied up inside the letters that follow, enclosed by them

parts.note: to elect is to vote someone in

explanation.surface: A government is constrained by a fresh ballot that calls for scrutiny.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oversight' suggests supervision, which fits the political surface, but here it means a lapse.
explanation.definitionFit: An oversight is a failure to notice or attend to something, which is neglect.

clue.text: Hand nannies primarily offer as security

parts.note: a paw is a jocular word for a hand

indicators.note: primarily means take only the first letter of the following word

parts.note: first letter of nannies

explanation.surface: Childminders hand something over as a guarantee.
explanation.definitionFit: To pawn an item is to deposit it with a lender as a pledge against a loan.

clue.text: Concealing king, rummy partners trick player

indicators.note: the rearranged letters hide the king's letter inside them
rummy means odd or strange, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: K is the abbreviation for king in chess and cards

explanation.surface: Card players at a rummy game hide a king to win a trick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rummy' and 'trick' both suggest a card table; 'rummy' signals the mix-up of PARTNERS and K goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A prankster is a practical joker, someone who plays tricks on others.

clue.text: Idler sentry forgetting uniform needs belt on

indicators.note: in a down clue, the belt sits on top of the remaining letters

parts.note: to slug is to hit hard, to belt

indicators.note: forgetting means the letter is left out

parts.note: a guard is a sentry
U is uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A lazy sentry, having left his uniform behind, needs to put a belt on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Belt' looks like part of the uniform, but it is the verb meaning to hit.
explanation.definitionFit: A sluggard is a lazy, slow-moving person, someone who habitually avoids work.

clue.text: Pleased the worst grade ignored in clearing?

indicators.note: the worst grade is left out, disregarded, from the word for a clearing

parts.note: a glade is a clearing in a wood
E is the lowest pass grade in exams

explanation.surface: A student is relieved that the bottom mark was overlooked.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'clearing' is a woodland glade, not the British university admissions scramble that the exam surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: Glad and pleased are synonyms, both meaning happy about something.

clue.text: Piano piece old double act put in the wrong order

indicators.note: the letters are rearranged out of sequence

parts.note: double supplies a second copy of the word act beside it
taken as written

explanation.surface: An old comedy pair perform their routine in muddled sequence.
explanation.definitionFit: A toccata is a virtuoso composition for a keyboard instrument, often for organ or piano.

clue.text: Show lion perhaps crossing plain

indicators.note: the animal's letters stretch across and around the other word

parts.note: a lion is an example of a big cat
plain means unadorned, bare

explanation.surface: A lion is seen making its way across open grassland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plain' looks like the savannah but means unadorned.
explanation.definitionFit: A cabaret is a nightclub entertainment of songs, dance and comedy, a kind of stage performance.

clue.text: Well-meaning concern for children having fun cycling around rocks

indicators.note: the cycled letters go around the word for rocks
cycling moves the first letter of the word round to its end

parts.note: on the rocks means with ice, so rocks is ice

explanation.surface: A children's charity has fun cycling around a rocky landscape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rocks' means ice, as in a drink served on the rocks; 'cycling' is not a bike ride but sends a letter round from front to back.
explanation.definitionFit: UNICEF is the United Nations agency for children's welfare, a charitable organisation, as concern means business.

clue.text: Revolutionary toasted aged monarch after Spooner

indicators.note: in the manner of Reverend Spooner, who swapped the opening sounds of words

parts.note: browned, as bread is in a toaster; said aloud, browned sounds like bround
a grey king, a monarch whose hair has whitened with age; said aloud, grey king sounds like greaking

explanation.surface: An elderly king is described as browned by the sun and revolutionary.
explanation.walkthrough: Say 'browned grey king' with the opening sounds swapped and it becomes 'ground breaking'.
explanation.definitionFit: Groundbreaking work is innovative and pioneering, overturning what went before, so revolutionary.

clue.text: Pipe fitting is round, as it happens

parts.note: O is round in shape
a live broadcast goes out as it happens

explanation.surface: A plumber remarks on the shape of a pipe joint.
explanation.walkthrough: An olive is a small brass ring in a compression joint in plumbing.
explanation.definitionFit: In plumbing an olive is a brass compression ring that seals a pipe joint when the nut is tightened.

clue.text: Chinese leader after Mao, almost as long

indicators.note: the Chinese leader's letters come after those from Mao
almost means the final letter of the name is lost

parts.note: Xi Jinping is the leader of China

explanation.surface: A historical note on the succession of China's leaders after Chairman Mao.
explanation.definitionFit: Maxi describes a garment, such as a skirt or coat, reaching the ankles: full-length.

clue.text: Risky flying BA when carrying blue bags

indicators.note: the word for when holds everything else between its letters

parts.note: as means when, as in 'as I left'

indicators.note: the word for blue captures the airline initials, holding them inside

parts.note: blue means risqué, so erotic

explanation.surface: A British Airways crew carries luggage during a hair-raising flight.
explanation.walkthrough: BA is British Airways, kept as written; 'bags' looks like luggage but signals containment.
explanation.definitionFit: Aerobatics are stunts performed in an aircraft, such as loops and rolls, which involve daring manoeuvres.

clue.text: Broken down old Ford model, a large vehicle

indicators.note: down in the sense of lacking or short of, as in 'down a player', so a letter goes

parts.note: bust means broken
the Model T was an early Ford car

explanation.surface: A vintage Ford breaks down, and so does a big vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broken down' reads as one phrase, but 'Broken' gives BUST and 'down' means short of the T.
explanation.definitionFit: A bus is a large road vehicle carrying many passengers.

clue.text: Disciple following Jesus around with Matthew, Mark, etc

parts.note: AD, Anno Domini, labels the years after the birth of Christ
around in the sense of present, as in 'is she around?', so here
the Gospels of Matthew and Mark are books of the New Testament, NT

explanation.surface: A follower of Jesus keeps company with the Gospel writers.
explanation.definitionFit: An adherent is a supporter or follower of a leader or cause, as a disciple is of a teacher.

clue.text: A man who's not at all smart, namely Trump

definitions.text: A man who's not at all smart

parts.note: sc. (scilicet) is the abbreviation meaning namely
in card games to ruff is to trump

explanation.surface: A jibe that a certain scruffy-looking man is in fact Trump.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trump' reads as the politician but is the card-game verb; 'not at all smart' means badly dressed, not stupid.
explanation.definitionFit: A scruff is an untidy, shabbily dressed person, the opposite of someone well turned out.
